title: UPDATE: Calgary police officer cleared in June police shooting
article: There will be no charges laid against a Calgary police officer who shot and killed a local man in June.
Corwin Peeace, 40, was shot four times in his southeast home, and pronounced dead on scene.
The incident began when police were called to a home in Erinwoods on June 10th.
They arrived on the doorstop within minutes of a 911 hang up call.
A woman had said she was in distress, and a man could be heard in the background threatening her.
Moments after police arrived, they were confronted with a man wielding a knife.
The head of the Calgary Police Association says the officer had no choice but to use deadly force.
However, an ASIRT investigation is always held when an officer is involved in a shooting, to make sure procedures were followed and there was no wrong-doing.
